items.headline: Mountain View council agenda: emergency declaration for 2026-27 El Niño
items.summary: The November 10 City Council agenda listed an emergency declaration and funding appropriation to prepare for the 2026-27 El Niño climate pattern. An El Niño update was also on the agenda.

items.headline: Council agenda: limits on watering decorative turfgrass with drinking water
items.summary: The November 10 agenda listed code amendments restricting potable (drinking-quality) water irrigation of nonfunctional turfgrass. The same item would update the city's recycled water service area.

items.headline: Council agenda: rowhouse project at 924-940 San Rafael Avenue
items.summary: The November 10 agenda listed the Rowhouse Gatekeeper Project at 924-940 San Rafael Avenue. A gatekeeper review is an early step in the city's process for proposals that would need a change to the General Plan or zoning.

items.headline: Council agenda: Justin Mates proposed as new city attorney
items.summary: The November 10 agenda listed the appointment of a City Attorney and authorization to execute an employment agreement with Justin Mates.

items.headline: Council agenda: proposed rule changes for city parks and facilities
items.summary: The November 10 agenda listed amendments to Chapter 38 of the City Code, which regulates the use of city parks and other city facilities. The same agenda included the Climate Forward Plan and the 2024 community greenhouse gas emissions inventory.

items.headline: Silicon Valley Power software contract listed at up to $3.79M
items.summary: The November 10 City Council agenda listed an action to let the City Manager sign an agreement with cQuant.io, Inc. for generation resource modeling software for Silicon Valley Power. Maximum compensation was $3,791,855 over a ten-year term.

items.headline: Eden Housing's 251-unit project at 10333 N. Wolfe on Planning Commission agenda
items.summary: The November 10 Planning Commission agenda listed architectural and site approval and a tree removal permit for Eden Housing's 251-unit residential development at 10333 N. Wolfe Road. The plan includes site and trail improvements and the removal and replacement of 117 protected trees.

items.headline: 363-unit apartment plan to replace Stevens Creek Blvd offices on agenda
items.summary: The November 10 Planning Commission agenda listed The Hanover Company's proposal for a 363-unit apartment development at 19220-19300 Stevens Creek Boulevard, replacing existing office buildings. The site is on Sites 5 and 6 of the city's Priority Housing Sites in the 6th Cycle Housing Element, and the project uses SB 330 and State Density Bonus law.
